title: Gunfire as Escorts Foil Attempted Robbery of C5 Coordinator Salvador Guerrero Chiprés in Colonia Juárez
detail: C5 (Centro de Comando, Control, Cómputo, Comunicaciones y Contacto Ciudadano) coordinator general Salvador Guerrero Chiprés was traveling with three SSC escorts at the intersection of Abraham González and Avenida Morelos, in the Juárez neighborhood, Cuauhtémoc borough, on the afternoon of August 11 when two men attempted to rob the vehicle. His escorts got out and fired shots to deter the assailants, then pursued and detained one — a 24-year-old man found carrying a replica firearm and a cell phone. He was read his rights and turned over to the Ministerio Público. Guerrero Chiprés was unharmed and went on to attend a scheduled public event at the Zócalo with Jefa de Gobierno Clara Brugada.

title: Storms Flood Reforma and Chapultepec Corridors, Fell Trees Across 13 of 16 Alcaldías
detail: Heavy rain on the afternoon and evening of August 11 caused flooding, waterlogged streets, and traffic disruption across Mexico City. The Secretaría de Gestión Integral de Riesgos y Protección Civil (SGIRPC) activated a Yellow Alert in 13 of the city's 16 alcaldías. Flooding on Paseo de la Reforma blocked pedestrian crossings and backed up traffic toward Chapultepec; the Secretaría de Gestión Integral del Agua (Segiagua) responded to flooding on Calle Antonio Alzate in the Agricultura neighborhood, Miguel Hidalgo, while Avenida Constituyentes toward Avenida Marina Nacional saw slow-moving traffic from 8:00 p.m. The Sistema de Transporte Colectivo activated slow-speed safety protocols on Metro Lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, and 12 and Line B. Fire crews also responded to fallen trees and short-circuits caused by the storm; no deaths were reported.

media.caption: Firefighters respond to fallen trees and flooding as storms swept Mexico City on August 11
